4. The AMQP integration schema (U4) will be defined as a Mule configuration XSD, aligned with Mule's standard XML configuration structure to ensure native IDE autocomplete and syntax validation support.
5. The base project skeleton (U5) will be delivered as a Maven archetype, following MuleSoft's recommended project structure for Mule 4 applications.
6. Centralized AMQP transport configuration (U6) will be implemented using Mule's global element configuration pattern, allowing common transport attributes to be defined once and referenced across all flows and applications.
7. Continuous AMQP message consumption (U7) will use the AMQP connector's persistent listener source with automatic acknowledgment, integrated with Mule's event processing pipeline to deliver messages to flows as they arrive.
8. Instant on-demand AMQP message consumption (U8) will use the AMQP connector's request-reply operation pattern, enabling synchronous message consumption at any point in a Mule flow.

technical_and_design_decisions: Mule 4 runtime will be used as the base platform for all implementation, leveraging its native ESB capabilities and Runtime Manager APIs for deployment operations.

The official MuleSoft AMQP connector will be extended (rather than built from scratch) to implement all AMQP-related user stories, reducing development effort and ensuring compatibility with standard AMQP brokers.
The DeploymentService for domain and application management will wrap existing Mule Runtime Manager REST APIs to provide the required deployment, undeployment, and redeployment functionality.
The AMQP integration schema (U4) will be defined as a Mule configuration XSD, aligned with Mule's standard XML configuration structure to ensure native IDE autocomplete and syntax validation support.
The base project skeleton (U5) will be delivered as a Maven archetype, following MuleSoft's recommended project structure for Mule 4 applications.

Centralized AMQP transport configuration (U6) will be implemented using Mule's global element configuration pattern, allowing common transport attributes to be defined once and referenced across all flows and applications.

Continuous AMQP message consumption (U7) will use the AMQP connector's persistent listener source with automatic acknowledgment, integrated with Mule's event processing pipeline to deliver messages to flows as they arrive.
Instant on-demand AMQP message consumption (U8) will use the AMQP connector's request-reply operation pattern, enabling synchronous message consumption at any point in a Mule flow.
assumptions: The development team has prior experience with Mule 4 development, Maven, AMQP protocol, and MuleSoft connector extension.
A standard AMQP broker (e.g., RabbitMQ) test environment is pre-provisioned, accessible, and configured with required permissions for testing AMQP functionality.
Mule Runtime Manager REST API endpoints are fully documented, accessible, and support all required operations for domain and application deployment management.
Target IDE support for the AMQP schema is limited to IntelliJ IDEA and Eclipse, the most commonly used IDEs for Mule development.
No custom security, authentication, or authorization requirements are specified for the deployment services or AMQP transport, so standard Mule and AMQP authentication mechanisms will be used.
The base project skeleton will only support Mule 4.x runtime versions, as older Mule runtime versions are end-of-life and not in scope.

Develop the DeploymentService module to support domain deployment, undeployment of domains and all associated applications, and domain redeployment with automatic app updates, leveraging Mule Runtime Manager APIs as per U1.
